title: A bound on list order counts
statement: Let $l$ be a finite list in a linearly ordered type. For each entry $x$ of $l$, count the entries strictly below $x$ and the entries strictly above $x$. The sum over the entries of the larger of these two counts, multiplied by $4$, is at most $3|l|^2$, where $|l|$ is the length of $l$.
hypotheses_covered: The entries belong to a linearly ordered type
